biorxiv-medrxiv.purpose: bioRxiv/medRxiv preprint discovery — critical for Conference Synthesis Brief deliverables where peer-reviewed publication is months away. Load-bearing for early-signal detection in Failed Trial Archaeology. CAPABILITY COVERED SINCE 2026-09-19 WITHOUT THIS ADAPTER — do not build one for topical search, it cannot work. bioRxiv's own API has NO keyword/author/full-text search (date-range and category listing only, re-verified live 2026-09-19), so a dedicated bioRxiv fetcher could never serve a role prefetch, which is topical by construction. Europe PMC indexes the same preprints AND is keyword-searchable, so the capability is served by the `europepmc-preprints` local fetcher (bound to scout and literature_reviewer), which returns preprint DOIs (verified: 1,890 bioRxiv-specific hits for glioblastoma vs 4,252 preprints overall). Because those records are DOI-bearing they also feed the Phase-30 grounding gate, which a bioRxiv-only adapter would have done no better. NB this was FIRST attempted as a config-only prefetch entry appending 'AND SRC:PPR' to EuropePMC_search_articles' query template; that is broken and must not be reinstated — a template with a literal tail is never empty, which defeats tool-prefetch's empty-args skip guard AND its topic fallback, so a topic-only template would search the bare filter clause. What remains genuinely unavailable this way is bioRxiv-specific metadata (per-server posting statistics, funder listings, version history) — build the adapter only if a deliverable actually needs those, not for search.
biorxiv-medrxiv.suggested_adapter_path: n/a for search — covered by the europepmc-preprints local fetcher (built 2026-09-19). patsnap.citation_gap: BLOCKING for engine use, but via INVISIBILITY, not deflation. openclaw-bridge/core/citation-extractor.js:3-27 recognizes exactly seven identifier types — PMID, PubChem CID, NCT, UniProt, ChEMBL, DrugBank, DOI. A patent publication number (e.g. US12458612B2) matches NONE, so it is never extracted into the cited set: not grounded against runtime-retrieved records, not Crossref retraction-screened, and neither raising nor lowering the citation-integrity grade because it was never counted in it. Consequence 1: the tagline's 'Every citation, checked.' does NOT extend to patent assertions (SYSTEM-REALITY.md:15). Consequence 2 — THE REAL CUSTOMER RISK, and it is the opposite of deflation: a buyer sees an A grade on deliverables/citation-integrity.md sitting beside a patent section and reasonably concludes the patents were graded. They were never counted. Any bundle mixing the two needs an explicit grade-adjacency disclosure. Closing the gap means adding a PATENT pattern to CITATION_PATTERNS PLUS a runtime patent-id grounding source IN THE SAME CHANGE — a pattern without a fetched-id set is the ordering that genuinely deflates, because every patent citation would then report ungrounded and reports would start failing.

ctgov-supplemental.purpose: Stop-reason archaeology. Searches ClinicalTrials.gov v2 for TERMINATED/WITHDRAWN/SUSPENDED trials in a condition and returns nctId, overallStatus, phases, the sponsor's whyStopped text, and protocol change-history (version count + most-amended modules). TWO MODES since 2026-07-30, deliberately asymmetric: PROMPT mode (default) is a single page hard-clamped at 50 records because its output is injected into an agent prompt, where size is cost; CENSUS mode (census:true) walks nextPageToken to the end of the result set for the post-gate deliverable, whose output is written to a file and never reaches a prompt. The session cache key carries the mode and sizes so the two can never serve each other, and scripts/_workflow-runtime.js additionally forces census:false AND clamps pageSize on the prefetch seam.
ctgov-supplemental.health_check: searchStoppedTrials({condition:'glioblastoma', census:true}) returns 390 records with eligibleTotal 390 and censusComplete true (~7 s incl. 40 history calls); searchStoppedTrials({condition:'glioblastoma', pageSize:1000}) returns at MOST 50 — the prompt-path ceiling must not follow the census ceiling.
ctgov-supplemental.registry_note: Was in tool-prefetch-map.json but declared in NO registry entry — the audit's 'tools in prefetch but not declared' drift. Declared 2026-07-24.
ctgov-supplemental.coverage_semantics: countTotal=true on page 1 is the ONLY true denominator — pageSize is silently clamped at 1000 (verified: pageSize=1001 returned HTTP 200 with 1000 studies and a byte-identical body), so a short page is never an error signal and studies.length is a floor. censusComplete is true ONLY when the walk ended cleanly with no error AND the collected count reached countTotal; a clean-but-short walk reports the gap and refuses to name a single cause. Completeness is bound to the CONDITION QUERY, never to the disease: query.cond is term-matched, and measured 2026-07-30 'NSCLC' returns 1,401 records where 'non-small cell lung cancer' returns 1,391.
ctgov-supplemental.history_bound: Change-history is strictly ONE HTTP CALL PER NCT — every batch shape tested returned 400/404 and the published v2 data model exposes no history field. Median 103 ms. Bounded at 40 in census mode (5 in prompt mode) at concurrency 3 with 400 ms inter-batch pauses: 40 calls = 6,852 ms, 0 non-200, and that is the LARGEST sweep actually measured. Do NOT raise it on arithmetic alone — sustained behaviour past ~40 consecutive calls against the undocumented /api/int endpoint is not established.
ctgov-supplemental.why_census_shipped: CORRECTNESS, not enhancement. buildAmendmentRisk derives LOW/MODERATE/HIGH from the median version count of the sample. Measured 2026-07-30 on one ordered glioblastoma cohort the shipped code returned MODERATE at n=5, MODERATE at n=8, LOW at n=10, MODERATE at n=20 and HIGH at n=40 — the band in a $14,950 deliverable was a function of sample size, not of the indication. The band is still climbing at n=40, so the memo now states its sample size and the band's sensitivity rather than implying the number is settled.

ctgov-design-benchmark.purpose: Comparative Phase 3 trial STRUCTURE. Searches ClinicalTrials.gov v2 for the comparable-program cohort in an indication and returns, per program, allocation / masking / intervention model / primary purpose / arm count / enrollment count+type / primary outcome measures with timeframes / lead sponsor + sponsor class / start + primary-completion dates — all in ONE search call, no per-study round-trip. Sibling of ctgov-supplemental (which asks what DIED and why); this asks how the survivors are BUILT. Session-cached, and the SAME instance backs both role prefetch and the workflow engine's post-gate render so deliverables/design-benchmark.{md,csv} render from exactly the records the analyst was grounded on. This is the fulfillment path for the Trial Design Benchmark Pack ($4,950) — before 2026-07-30 that SKU had no template, no mission template and no intake path.
ctgov-design-benchmark.selection_rule: EXPLICIT AND PART OF THE PRODUCT. Sends filter.overallStatus=COMPLETED,ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING,RECRUITING,ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION and sort=StartDate:desc, and returns both to the renderer, which prints them. Verified live 2026-07-30: the unfiltered query reports totalCount 1014 for non-small cell lung cancer and the filtered one 668 — so ~34% of an unfiltered 'eligible' denominator would be withdrawn/terminated/suspended/unknown or never started, and an unsorted page returned a 1995 trial with status UNKNOWN plus a WITHDRAWN trial with enrollment 0. A stated slice is the deliverable; an arbitrary page is not.

sec-edgar.purpose: SEC EDGAR full-text search over public-company filings. Added 2026-09-19 to close a gap the GRADING layer already anticipated: gate.config.js has listed sec.gov in primary_source_domains since 2026-07-07, but nothing ever fetched it and a name search across all 2,116 ToolUniverse tools returns ZERO SEC coverage. Supplies a signal no biomedical database carries -- a sponsor's own filed disclosure that a program was discontinued, a trial failed, or a partnership ended. SCOPE, verified live: EDGAR full-text returns filing METADATA ONLY (no snippet or highlight field), so a record says WHICH filing matched, never WHAT it said; it does carry the standardized 8-K item codes, which are decoded to their SEC-defined meanings (2.02 = Results of Operations, 1.02 = Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement, ...) and an unmapped code renders bare rather than being given an invented label. CONTEXT-ONLY BY DESIGN: accession numbers are not in citation-extractor.js's grammar -- every pattern there requires a literal prefix (PMID/CID/NCT/UniProt/CHEMBL/DB/doi:), verified by reading them -- so these records cannot enter the grounded-ratio denominator, cannot lower a report's grade, and never reach the Stage-3 re-resolver (where an unknown id type risks UNRESOLVED, a hard BLOCK). Making SEC filings citable would mean extending citation-extractor.js AND citation-reresolver.js in one change; deliberately deferred. UPDATE 2026-10-21: on the BUSINESS research profile only, openclaw-bridge/mcp/business-sources/sec-filings.js (entry sec-filings-citable) wraps this fetcher and renders filings citable as `SEC: <CIK>/<accession>`, with matching patterns in citation-extractor.js and a resolver in citation-reresolver.js: the deferred change, made for that profile. On the biomedical profile this entry is unchanged and stays context-only.

europepmc-preprints.auth: none (public Europe PMC REST; polite User-Agent with contact email sent)
europepmc-preprints.purpose: Preprint lane via Europe PMC, restricted with SRC:PPR. Built 2026-09-19 to serve the capability the `biorxiv-medrxiv` entry describes as 'critical for Conference Synthesis Brief' and 'load-bearing for early-signal detection in Failed Trial Archaeology'. bioRxiv's own API has NO keyword/author/full-text search (date-range and category listing only, re-verified live 2026-09-19), so a bioRxiv-specific adapter could never serve a role prefetch, which is topical by construction; Europe PMC indexes the same preprints and is keyword-searchable. WHY A FETCHER AND NOT A CONFIG LINE (this was attempted first and is a trap worth recording): appending 'AND SRC:PPR' to a prefetch-map query template produces a string that is never empty, which defeats BOTH tool-prefetch.js's empty-args skip guard -- so an empty input set spends a call on a bare filter clause -- AND its topic fallback, which substitutes `topic` only into an exactly-empty argument, so general-research-pack would have searched ' AND SRC:PPR'. EuropePMC_search_articles exposes no source/preprint parameter to move the filter into, so config could not express it. Composing the query in code fixes both. plugin_surfaces.rationale: Ledger of every Claude PLUGIN bound to this business. A plugin is not a connector — it is a bundle of skills plus (usually) a set of MCP servers. plugin_surfaces.placeholder_model: Plugin packages ship generic `~~category` placeholders (203 across the installed set) that each deployment resolves to its own tools.
